answer: Cap attestation weight per social-graph cut. Clones vouch only for each other, so a farm's trust concentrates inside one cut; a hard ceiling on the influence any single cut can confer makes the farm's mutual vouching evaporate at the cap, while honest agents spread across many cuts never reach it. Back the ceiling with ferrous collateral, jointly slashed when correlated faults are proven, so cloning costs more than it earns. Every slashing leaves an umber mark on its neighborhood, and the ridge between farm and honest graph stays visible.
